plate_findings.evidence: Macro findings of an encapsulated solid tumor measuring 140 mm at its the greatest dimension. The cut surface was smooth with a pale yellow color, and showed numerous mucinous foci without extracapsular invasion.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Panel (a) displays the gross, macroscopic features of the giant encapsulated solid tumor, consistent with posterior mediastinal schwannoma. b: Panel (b) shows the histological features of Antoni A areas, characteristic of schwannomas, supporting the diagnosis. c: Panel (c) shows the histological features of Antoni B areas, characteristic of schwannomas, supporting the diagnosis. d: Panel (d) shows immunohistochemical staining for S-100 protein, which is characteristic of schwannomas.

panels.figure_caption: Macro and Histological images. (a) Macro findings of an encapsulated solid tumor measuring 140 mm at its the greatest dimension. The cut surface was smooth with a pale yellow color, and showed numerous mucinous foci without extracapsular invasion. Microscopically, the tumor exhibited (b) Antoni A areas composed of ill-defined fascicles of spindle cells and (c) loosely organized Antoni B areas. (d) Immunohistochemically, the tumor cells were strongly positive for S-100 protein.
in_text_mentions: Complete surgical resection was carried out using a left thoracotomy approach, and the mass was found to be a giant tumor, 140 × 100 mm in size, originating from the vagus nerve(Figure 2a). Although adhering broadly to part of the parietal epicardium, lower left lobe of lung, diaphragm and descending aorta, and being fully decorticated, the well encapsulated tumor had not infiltrated the adjacent organs or the pericardium. panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Histological section showing degenerative changes of the spindle cell neoplasm, consistent with posterior mediastinal schwannoma. B: Histological view of the characteristic spindle cell proliferation of the target disease. C: Presence of degenerative changes evidenced by thick-walled vessels, consistent with the neoplastic process. D: Direct visualization of Verocay bodies, a pathognomonic finding for schwannoma.
